source.text: וַיִּהְיוּ֙ חַיֵּ֣י שָׂרָ֔ה מֵאָ֥ה שָׁנָ֛ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וְשֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֑ים שְׁנֵ֖י חַיֵּ֥י שָׂרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And were [the] life of Sarah a hundred year[s] and twenty year[s] and seven years; [the] years of [the] life of Sarah.

en.L: And the life of Sarah was 127 years; [these were] the years of the life of Sarah.
en.B: Sarah lived to the age of 127; those were the years of her life.
en.R: Sarah lived to be 127 years old.

es.L: Y la vida de Sara fue de ciento veintisiete años; [estos fueron] los años de la vida de Sara.
es.B: Sara vivió hasta los ciento veintisiete años; esos fueron los años de su vida.
es.R: Sara vivió ciento veintisiete años.

fr.L: Et la vie de Sara fut de cent vingt-sept ans ; [ce furent] les années de la vie de Sara.
fr.B: Sara vécut jusqu’à l’âge de cent vingt-sept ans ; telles furent les années de sa vie.
fr.R: Sara a vécu jusqu’à cent vingt-sept ans.

sw.L: Na maisha ya Sara yalikuwa miaka mia moja na ishirini na saba; [hiyo ndiyo] miaka ya maisha ya Sara.
sw.B: Sara aliishi miaka mia moja na ishirini na saba; hiyo ndiyo miaka ya maisha yake.
sw.R: Sara aliishi mpaka umri wa miaka mia moja na ishirini na saba.

decisions.choice: the years of the life of Sarah: a solemn closing phrase
decisions.reason: The verse names Sarah's life at its start and again at its end, framing her age like a short epitaph. Sarah is the only woman in the Bible whose age at death is recorded.

decisions.choice: passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("fut", "vécut"); passé composé at Readable ("a vécu")
decisions.reason: As the French style guide sets for narrative: the passé simple is the tense of written French narrative; Readable uses the passé composé, the tense of spoken French and of school reading today. Speech keeps the tenses of speech at every level.

source.text: וַתָּ֣מָת שָׂרָ֗ה בְּקִרְיַ֥ת אַרְבַּ֛ע הִ֥וא חֶבְר֖וֹן בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן וַיָּבֹא֙ אַבְרָהָ֔ם לִסְפֹּ֥ד לְשָׂרָ֖ה וְלִבְכֹּתָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And died Sarah in Kiriath-arba, that [is] Hebron, in [the] land of Canaan; and came Abraham to mourn for Sarah and to weep for her.

en.L: And Sarah died in Kiriath-arba, that [is], Hebron, in the land of Canaan; and Abraham came to mourn for Sarah and to weep for her.
en.B: She died at Kiriath-arba, the place now called Hebron, in the land of Canaan, and Abraham went in to mourn for Sarah and weep over her.
en.R: She died in Kiriath-arba, which is Hebron, in the land of Canaan. Abraham went to grieve for Sarah and cry over her.

es.L: Y murió Sara en Quiriat-arbá, que [es] Hebrón, en la tierra de Canaán; y vino Abraham a hacer duelo por Sara y a llorarla.
es.B: Murió en Quiriat-arbá, el lugar que ahora se llama Hebrón, en la tierra de Canaán, y Abraham entró a hacer duelo por Sara y a llorar por ella.
es.R: Murió en Quiriat-arbá, que es Hebrón, en la tierra de Canaán. Abraham fue a llorar a Sara y a lamentar su muerte.

fr.L: Et Sara mourut à Kiryath-Arba, qui [est] Hébron, dans le pays de Canaan ; et Abraham vint pour faire le deuil de Sara et pour la pleurer.
fr.B: Elle mourut à Kiryath-Arba, le lieu qu’on appelle aujourd’hui Hébron, dans le pays de Canaan, et Abraham entra pour mener le deuil de Sara et la pleurer.
fr.R: Elle est morte à Kiryath-Arba, c’est-à-dire Hébron, dans le pays de Canaan. Abraham est allé auprès d’elle pour montrer son chagrin et la pleurer.

sw.L: Na Sara akafa huko Kiriath-arba, ambayo [ni] Hebroni, katika nchi ya Kanaani; na Abrahamu akaja kumwombolezea Sara na kumlilia.
sw.B: Alifariki huko Kiriath-arba, mahali panapoitwa sasa Hebroni, katika nchi ya Kanaani, naye Abrahamu akaingia kumwombolezea Sara na kumlilia.
sw.R: Alifariki huko Kiriath-arba, yaani Hebroni, katika nchi ya Kanaani. Abrahamu akaenda kuomboleza kwa ajili ya Sara na kumlilia.

decisions.choice: Kiriath-arba: "town of Arba" or "town of four", the older name of Hebron
decisions.reason: Joshua 14:15 says Arba was a great man among the Anakim; the name can also mean "town of four". The narrator gives the later name, Hebron, so readers know the place.

decisions.choice: came to mourn and to weep: formal mourning for the dead
decisions.reason: The verb "came" may mean that Abraham entered Sarah's tent to begin the rites of mourning, or that he came from Beersheba, where 22:19 last placed him. Mourning included loud weeping and lament.

source.text: וַיָּ֨קָם֙ אַבְרָהָ֔ם מֵעַ֖ל פְּנֵ֣י מֵת֑וֹ וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר אֶל־בְּנֵי־חֵ֖ת לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And rose Abraham from upon [the] face of his dead and spoke to [the] sons of Heth, saying,

en.L: And Abraham rose up from before his dead and spoke to the sons of Heth, saying,
en.B: Then Abraham rose from beside his dead wife and spoke to the Hittites.
en.R: Then Abraham got up from beside Sarah's body and went to speak with the Hittites, the people who lived there.

es.L: Y se levantó Abraham de delante de su muerta y habló a los hijos de Het, diciendo:
es.B: Luego Abraham se levantó de junto a su esposa muerta y habló con los hititas.
es.R: Después Abraham se levantó de al lado del cuerpo de Sara y fue a hablar con los hititas, la gente que vivía allí.

fr.L: Et Abraham se leva de devant sa morte et parla aux fils de Heth, disant :
fr.B: Puis Abraham se releva d’auprès de sa femme morte et s’adressa aux Hittites.
fr.R: Ensuite, Abraham a quitté le corps de Sara et il est allé parler aux Hittites, les gens qui habitaient là.

sw.L: Na Abrahamu akainuka kutoka mbele ya maiti yake, akasema na wana wa Hethi, akisema,
sw.B: Kisha Abrahamu akainuka kutoka kando ya mkewe aliyekufa, akazungumza na Wahiti.
sw.R: Kisha Abrahamu akainuka kutoka kando ya mwili wa Sara, akaenda kuzungumza na Wahiti, watu walioishi huko.

decisions.choice: the sons of Heth: the Hittites of Hebron
alternatives: the Hittite empire of Asia Minor
decisions.reason: "Sons of Heth" means the people descended from Heth, a son of Canaan (10:15). They were a local Canaanite people living around Hebron, probably not the same as the great Hittite empire to the north.

decisions.choice: the Hittites
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the people's name; Literal keeps "sons of Heth".

decisions.choice: speech begins in the next verse
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable end the sentence here and open Abraham's words in verse 4.

decisions.choice: "su muerta" (L), and "mi muerta" / "tu difunta" in the speeches that follow
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "his dead" is a general masculine form, but Spanish must give the noun a gender, and the dead one is Sarah; the masculine "su muerto" would read as a man. Literal keeps "muerta", Balanced uses the gentler "difunta" in the speeches, and Readable names her as "esposa" where the English Readable says "wife".

decisions.choice: "sa morte", and "ma morte" / "ta morte" in the speeches that follow
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "his dead" is a general masculine form, but French must give the noun a gender, and the dead one is Sarah; "son mort" would read as a man. Readable says "ma femme", "ta femme" where the English Readable says "wife".

source.text: גֵּר־וְתוֹשָׁ֥ב אָנֹכִ֖י עִמָּכֶ֑ם תְּנ֨וּ לִ֤י אֲחֻזַּת־קֶ֨בֶר֙ עִמָּכֶ֔ם וְאֶקְבְּרָ֥ה מֵתִ֖י מִלְּפָנָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: A sojourner and a resident I [am] with you; give to me a possession of a grave with you, and I will bury my dead from before me.

en.L: "A sojourner and a resident [alien] I am with you. Give me a possession of a burial place with you, that I may bury my dead from before me."
en.B: "I am a foreigner living among you as a settler. Grant me a piece of land of my own for a grave here, so that I can carry my dead away and bury her."
en.R: He said, "I am a foreigner who lives among you. Let me have some land of my own for a grave, so that I can bury my wife."

es.L: «Extranjero y residente soy yo entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. {{plural_you:Denme|Dadme}} una propiedad de sepultura entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, para que sepulte a mi muerta de delante de mí».
es.B: «Soy un extranjero que vive entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} como residente. {{plural_you:Concédanme|Concededme}} aquí un terreno propio para una tumba, para que pueda llevarme a mi difunta y darle sepultura».
es.R: Les dijo: «Soy un extranjero que vive entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. {{plural_you:Déjenme|Dejadme}} tener un terreno mío para una tumba, para poder enterrar a mi esposa».

fr.L: « Immigré et résident, je le suis chez vous. Donnez-moi une propriété de sépulture chez vous, afin que j’enterre ma morte [en l’emportant] de devant moi. »
fr.B: « Je suis un étranger établi parmi vous. Accordez-moi ici un terrain à moi pour une tombe, afin que je puisse emporter ma morte et l’enterrer. »
fr.R: Il leur a dit : « Je suis un étranger qui vit chez vous. Laissez-moi avoir un terrain à moi pour une tombe, pour que je puisse enterrer ma femme. »

sw.L: "Mgeni na mkaaji [ni] mimi kati yenu. Nipeni milki ya mahali pa kuzikia kati yenu, ili nimzike maiti yangu [kumwondoa] mbele yangu."
sw.B: "Mimi ni mgeni ninayeishi kati yenu kama mkaaji. Nipeni hapa kipande cha ardhi kiwe changu kwa ajili ya kaburi, ili nimchukue maiti yangu nikamzike."
sw.R: Akasema, "Mimi ni mgeni ninayeishi kati yenu. Niruhusuni nipate ardhi yangu mwenyewe kwa ajili ya kaburi, ili nimzike mke wangu."

decisions.choice: a sojourner and a resident: a foreigner with no rights to land
decisions.reason: The ger lived among a people not his own; the toshav was a settled resident who still did not belong. Abraham, to whom God promised the whole land (17:8), owns none of it and must ask to buy a grave. The same pair of words describes Israel before God in Leviticus 25:23 and 1 Chronicles 29:15.

decisions.choice: a possession of a burial place: land owned outright
decisions.reason: "Possession" (achuzzah) is the word of 17:8, "an everlasting possession". Abraham asks not for the loan of a tomb but for land of his own, the first piece of the promised land he will hold.

decisions.choice: my wife
decisions.reason: Readable names the one who has died.

source.text: וַיַּעֲנ֧וּ בְנֵי־חֵ֛ת אֶת־אַבְרָהָ֖ם לֵאמֹ֥ר לֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And answered [the] sons of Heth Abraham, saying to him,

en.L: And the sons of Heth answered Abraham, saying to him,
en.B: The Hittites replied to Abraham,
en.R: The Hittites answered Abraham,

es.L: Y respondieron los hijos de Het a Abraham, diciéndole:
es.B: Los hititas le respondieron a Abraham:
es.R: Los hititas contestaron a Abraham:

fr.L: Et les fils de Heth répondirent à Abraham, lui disant :
fr.B: Les Hittites répondirent à Abraham :
fr.R: Les Hittites ont répondu à Abraham :

sw.L: Na wana wa Hethi wakamjibu Abrahamu, wakimwambia,
sw.B: Wahiti wakamjibu Abrahamu,
sw.R: Wahiti wakamwambia Abrahamu,

source.text: שְׁמָעֵ֣נוּ׀אֲדֹנִ֗י נְשִׂ֨יא אֱלֹהִ֤ים אַתָּה֙ בְּתוֹכֵ֔נוּ בְּמִבְחַ֣ר קְבָרֵ֔ינוּ קְבֹ֖ר אֶת־מֵתֶ֑ךָ אִ֣ישׁ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ אֶת־קִבְר֛וֹ לֹֽא־יִכְלֶ֥ה מִמְּךָ֖ מִקְּבֹ֥ר מֵתֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Hear us, my lord; a prince of God you [are] among us; in [the] choicest of our graves bury your dead; [no] man of us his grave not will withhold from you, from burying your dead.

en.L: "Hear us, my lord. You are a prince of God among us. Bury your dead in the choicest of our graves. None of us will withhold his grave from you, so that you may bury your dead."
en.B: "Listen to us, sir. You are a mighty prince living among us. Bury your dead in the best of our tombs. Not one of us will refuse you his tomb for burying your dead."
en.R: "Sir, listen to us. You are an important leader among us. You can bury your wife in the best of our tombs. Any of us would gladly let you use his tomb."

es.L: «Escúchanos, señor mío: un príncipe de Dios eres tú entre nosotros. En el mejor de nuestros sepulcros sepulta a tu muerta. Ninguno de nosotros te negará su sepulcro para que sepultes a tu muerta».
es.B: «Escúchanos, señor. Eres un príncipe poderoso que vive entre nosotros. Entierra a tu difunta en la mejor de nuestras tumbas. Ninguno de nosotros te negará su tumba para que entierres en ella a tu difunta».
es.R: «Escúchanos, señor. Tú eres un jefe importante entre nosotros. Puedes enterrar a tu esposa en la mejor de nuestras tumbas. Cualquiera de nosotros te prestaría con gusto su tumba».

fr.L: « Écoute-nous, mon seigneur : un prince de Dieu, voilà ce que tu es au milieu de nous. Dans le meilleur de nos tombeaux enterre ta morte. Aucun de nous ne te refusera son tombeau pour que tu enterres ta morte. »
fr.B: « Écoute-nous, seigneur. Tu es un prince puissant parmi nous. Enterre ta morte dans le plus beau de nos tombeaux. Pas un de nous ne te refusera son tombeau pour que tu y enterres ta morte. »
fr.R: « Écoute-nous, seigneur. Tu es un chef important chez nous. Tu peux enterrer ta femme dans la meilleure de nos tombes. N’importe lequel d’entre nous te prêtera volontiers sa tombe. »

sw.L: "Utusikie, bwana wangu: wewe [ni] mkuu wa Mungu kati yetu. Mzike maiti yako katika makaburi yetu yaliyo bora kabisa. Hakuna hata mmoja wetu atakayekunyima kaburi lake usimzike maiti yako."
sw.B: "Utusikilize, bwana. Wewe ni mkuu mwenye nguvu anayeishi kati yetu. Mzike maiti yako katika kaburi lililo bora kuliko yote kati ya makaburi yetu. Hakuna hata mmoja wetu atakayekunyima kaburi lake ili umzike humo maiti yako."
sw.R: "Tusikilize, bwana. Wewe ni kiongozi mkubwa kati yetu. Unaweza kumzika mke wako katika kaburi letu lililo bora kuliko yote. Yeyote kati yetu atafurahi kukuachia kaburi lake utumie."

decisions.choice: a prince of God: a mighty prince
alternatives: a prince of God (a leader favored by God)
decisions.reason: The word elohim can be used to make a phrase superlative, "a mighty prince" (compare 30:8, "mighty wrestlings"). It may also mean that they see God's favor on Abraham (21:22).

decisions.choice: bury your dead in our graves: a generous but careful offer
decisions.reason: The Hittites offer the use of their tombs, not land of his own. Their courtesy turns aside his request to own ground among them (verse 4).

decisions.choice: "tú" (escúchanos, eres, tu) addressed to Abraham, even with "señor"
decisions.reason: The Hittites, and Ephron after them, speak to Abraham with great courtesy, and modern Spanish would often use "usted" here. Spanish Bible speech uses "tú" to one person whatever the rank, as the Spanish of Genesis 1-14 does; the courtesy is carried by "señor" and the wording.

decisions.choice: "tu" addressed to Abraham, with "seigneur"
decisions.reason: As the French style guide sets, "tu" is used to one person and "vous" to several, whatever the rank; the courtesy of the Hittites and of Ephron is carried by "seigneur" and the wording. "Seigneur" is lowercase here: a polite title for a man, not God.

source.text: וַיָּ֧קָם אַבְרָהָ֛ם וַיִּשְׁתַּ֥חוּ לְעַם־הָאָ֖רֶץ לִבְנֵי־חֵֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And rose Abraham and bowed to [the] people of the land, to [the] sons of Heth.

en.L: And Abraham rose and bowed down to the people of the land, to the sons of Heth.
en.B: Then Abraham stood and bowed low before the people of the land, the Hittites.
en.R: Abraham stood up and bowed down in front of the Hittites, the people of that land.

es.L: Y se levantó Abraham y se inclinó ante el pueblo de la tierra, ante los hijos de Het.
es.B: Entonces Abraham se puso de pie e hizo una profunda reverencia ante la gente del país, los hititas.
es.R: Abraham se levantó y se inclinó delante de los hititas, la gente de aquella tierra.

fr.L: Et Abraham se leva et se prosterna devant le peuple du pays, devant les fils de Heth.
fr.B: Alors Abraham se leva et s’inclina profondément devant les gens du pays, les Hittites.
fr.R: Abraham s’est levé et il s’est incliné devant les Hittites, les gens de ce pays.

sw.L: Na Abrahamu akainuka, akainama mbele ya watu wa nchi, mbele ya wana wa Hethi.
sw.B: Kisha Abrahamu akasimama, akasujudu mbele ya wenyeji wa nchi, Wahiti.
sw.R: Abrahamu akasimama, akainama mbele ya Wahiti, watu wa nchi ile.

decisions.choice: the people of the land: the citizens with a say in public matters
decisions.reason: The phrase means the full members of the community, the landholders who gathered at the city gate (verse 10) to witness and approve a sale.

source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר אִתָּ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר אִם־יֵ֣שׁ אֶֽת־נַפְשְׁכֶ֗ם לִקְבֹּ֤ר אֶת־מֵתִי֙ מִלְּפָנַ֔י שְׁמָע֕וּנִי וּפִגְעוּ־לִ֖י בְּעֶפְר֥וֹן בֶּן־צֹֽחַר׃

records.literal_gloss: And he spoke with them, saying, if it is with your soul to bury my dead from before me, hear me and entreat for me Ephron, son of Zohar,

en.L: And he spoke with them, saying, "If it is your wish that I bury my dead from before me, hear me and plead for me with Ephron the son of Zohar,
en.B: He said to them, "If you are willing for me to bury my dead, then listen to me: speak on my behalf to Ephron son of Zohar,
en.R: He said to them, "If you really want to help me bury my wife, please ask Ephron son of Zohar for me.

es.L: Y habló con ellos, diciendo: «Si es {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} voluntad que yo sepulte a mi muerta de delante de mí, {{plural_you:escúchenme|escuchadme}} e {{plural_you:intercedan|interceded}} por mí ante Efrón hijo de Zohar,
es.B: Les dijo: «Si {{plural_you:están|estáis}} dispuestos a que yo entierre a mi difunta, {{plural_you:escúchenme|escuchadme}}: {{plural_you:hablen|hablad}} en mi favor con Efrón hijo de Zohar,
es.R: Les dijo: «Si de verdad {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} ayudarme a enterrar a mi esposa, por favor, {{plural_you:hablen|hablad}} por mí con Efrón hijo de Zohar.

fr.L: Et il parla avec eux, disant : « Si c’est votre volonté que j’enterre ma morte [en l’emportant] de devant moi, écoutez-moi et intercédez pour moi auprès d’Éphron, fils de Tsohar,
fr.B: Il leur dit : « Si vous êtes d’accord pour que j’enterre ma morte, alors écoutez-moi : parlez en ma faveur à Éphron, fils de Tsohar,
fr.R: Il leur a dit : « Si vous voulez vraiment m’aider à enterrer ma femme, s’il vous plaît, allez parler pour moi à Éphron, fils de Tsohar.

sw.L: Akasema nao, akisema, "Ikiwa ni nia yenu nimzike maiti yangu [kumwondoa] mbele yangu, nisikilizeni, mkaniombee kwa Efroni mwana wa Sohari,
sw.B: Akawaambia, "Ikiwa mko radhi nimzike maiti yangu, basi nisikilizeni: mnisemee kwa Efroni mwana wa Sohari,
sw.R: Akawaambia, "Kama kweli mnataka kunisaidia kumzika mke wangu, tafadhali mnisemee kwa Efroni mwana wa Sohari.

decisions.choice: if it is with your soul: if it is your will
decisions.reason: "Soul" (nefesh) here means desire or will: "if you are truly willing".

decisions.choice: plead for me with Ephron: a go-between in the sale
decisions.reason: Abraham does not approach the landowner directly but asks the assembly to speak for him, the polite way to open a sale before witnesses.

source.text: וְיִתֶּן־לִ֗י אֶת־מְעָרַ֤ת הַמַּכְפֵּלָה֙ אֲשֶׁר־ל֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֖ר בִּקְצֵ֣ה שָׂדֵ֑הוּ בְּכֶ֨סֶף מָלֵ֜א יִתְּנֶ֥נָּה לִ֛י בְּתוֹכְכֶ֖ם לַאֲחֻזַּת־קָֽבֶר׃

records.literal_gloss: and may he give to me [the] cave of the Machpelah which [is] to him, which [is] at [the] end of his field; for silver full let him give it to me among you for a possession of a grave.

en.L: that he may give me the cave of Machpelah which is his, which is at the end of his field. For the full price in silver let him give it to me among you as a possession for a burial place."
en.B: and ask him to let me have the cave of Machpelah that belongs to him, at the edge of his field. Let him sell it to me for its full price, here in your presence, as a burial place I can own."
en.R: I want him to sell me the cave of Machpelah at the far end of his field. I will pay him the full price in silver, here in front of you all. Then it will be my own place for a grave."

es.L: para que me dé la cueva de Macpela que es suya, que está al extremo de su campo. Por plata completa que me la dé entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} como propiedad de sepultura».
es.B: y {{plural_you:pídanle|pedidle}} que me deje la cueva de Macpela que le pertenece, al borde de su campo. Que me la venda por su precio completo, aquí delante de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, como sepultura que sea mía».
es.R: Quiero que me venda la cueva de Macpela, que está al fondo de su campo. Le pagaré en plata el precio completo, aquí delante de todos {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Así será un lugar mío para una tumba».

fr.L: pour qu’il me donne la caverne de Makpéla qui est à lui, qui est au bout de son champ. Pour [son] plein [prix en] argent, qu’il me la donne au milieu de vous comme propriété de sépulture. »
fr.B: et demandez-lui de me céder la caverne de Makpéla qui lui appartient, à l’extrémité de son champ. Qu’il me la vende à son plein prix, ici devant vous, comme un lieu de sépulture qui soit à moi. »
fr.R: Je voudrais qu’il me vende la grotte de Makpéla, tout au bout de son champ. Je lui paierai le prix complet en argent, ici devant vous tous. Comme ça, j’aurai à moi un endroit pour une tombe. »

sw.L: ili anipe pango la Makpela lililo lake, lililo mwisho wa shamba lake. Kwa fedha kamili na anipe kati yenu kuwa milki ya mahali pa kuzikia."
sw.B: na kumwomba aniachie pango la Makpela lililo lake, pembeni mwa shamba lake. Aniuzie kwa bei yake kamili, hapa mbele yenu, liwe mahali pa kuzikia palipo pangu mwenyewe."
sw.R: Nataka aniuzie pango la Makpela lililo upande wa mwisho wa shamba lake. Nitamlipa bei kamili kwa fedha, hapa mbele yenu nyote. Hapo litakuwa mahali pangu mwenyewe pa kaburi."

decisions.choice: Machpelah: probably "the double (cave)"
decisions.reason: The name has the article ("the Machpelah") and seems to come from a word for "double". It may describe a cave with two chambers. Later the name covers the whole area (verse 17).

decisions.choice: for full silver: at the full price
decisions.reason: Abraham insists on paying the full value so that the land is his beyond dispute (1 Chronicles 21:22, 24, where David says the same).

source.text: וְעֶפְר֥וֹן יֹשֵׁ֖ב בְּת֣וֹךְ בְּנֵי־חֵ֑ת וַיַּעַן֩ עֶפְר֨וֹן הַחִתִּ֤י אֶת־אַבְרָהָם֙ בְּאָזְנֵ֣י בְנֵי־חֵ֔ת לְכֹ֛ל בָּאֵ֥י שַֽׁעַר־עִיר֖וֹ לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And Ephron [was] sitting in [the] midst of [the] sons of Heth; and answered Ephron the Hittite Abraham in [the] ears of [the] sons of Heth, of all [those] entering [the] gate of his city, saying,

en.L: Now Ephron was sitting among the sons of Heth; and Ephron the Hittite answered Abraham in the hearing of the sons of Heth, all who went in at the gate of his city, saying,
en.B: Ephron himself was sitting there among the Hittites, and Ephron the Hittite answered Abraham so that all the Hittites who had come to the gate of his city could hear.
en.R: Ephron was sitting there with the other Hittites. He answered Abraham so that all the men at the city gate could hear.

es.L: Y Efrón estaba sentado en medio de los hijos de Het; y respondió Efrón el hitita a Abraham a oídos de los hijos de Het, de todos los que entraban por la puerta de su ciudad, diciendo:
es.B: Efrón mismo estaba sentado allí entre los hititas, y Efrón el hitita respondió a Abraham de modo que lo oyeran todos los hititas que habían venido a la puerta de su ciudad.
es.R: Efrón estaba sentado allí con los demás hititas. Le respondió a Abraham de manera que lo oyeran todos los hombres que estaban a la puerta de la ciudad.

fr.L: Or Éphron était assis au milieu des fils de Heth ; et Éphron le Hittite répondit à Abraham aux oreilles des fils de Heth, de tous ceux qui entraient par la porte de sa ville, disant :
fr.B: Éphron lui-même était assis là parmi les Hittites, et Éphron le Hittite répondit à Abraham de sorte que tous les Hittites venus à la porte de sa ville purent l’entendre.
fr.R: Éphron était assis là, avec les autres Hittites. Il a répondu à Abraham devant tous les hommes réunis à la porte de la ville, pour qu’ils entendent.

sw.L: Na Efroni alikuwa ameketi katikati ya wana wa Hethi; naye Efroni Mhiti akamjibu Abrahamu masikioni mwa wana wa Hethi, wa wote waliokuwa wakiingia katika lango la mji wake, akisema,
sw.B: Efroni mwenyewe alikuwa ameketi pale kati ya Wahiti, naye Efroni Mhiti akamjibu Abrahamu hivi kwamba Wahiti wote waliokuja langoni pa mji wake waliweza kusikia.
sw.R: Efroni alikuwa ameketi pale pamoja na Wahiti wengine. Akamjibu Abrahamu ili wanaume wote waliokuwa langoni pa mji wasikie.

decisions.choice: all who went in at the gate of his city: the town council
decisions.reason: The city gate was where the town's men gathered and where legal business was done before witnesses (Ruth 4:1-11). The phrase means the full citizens who had the right to sit in council there.

decisions.choice: all the men at the city gate
alternatives: all who went in at the gate
decisions.reason: Readable simplifies the phrase; those who sat in council at the gate were men.

source.text: לֹֽא־אֲדֹנִ֣י שְׁמָעֵ֔נִי הַשָּׂדֶה֙ נָתַ֣תִּי לָ֔ךְ וְהַמְּעָרָ֥ה אֲשֶׁר־בּ֖וֹ לְךָ֣ נְתַתִּ֑יהָ לְעֵינֵ֧י בְנֵי־עַמִּ֛י נְתַתִּ֥יהָ לָּ֖ךְ קְבֹ֥ר מֵתֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: No, my lord, hear me; the field I give to you, and the cave which [is] in it, to you I give it; to [the] eyes of [the] sons of my people I give it to you; bury your dead.

en.L: "No, my lord, hear me: I give you the field, and the cave that is in it I give to you. In the sight of the sons of my people I give it to you. Bury your dead."
en.B: "No, sir, listen to me. I am giving you the field, and the cave in it as well. Here, with my own people as witnesses, I make it yours. Go and bury your dead."
en.R: "No, sir, listen. I will give you the field, and the cave too. My people are my witnesses. It is yours. Go and bury your wife."

es.L: «No, señor mío, escúchame: el campo te lo doy, y la cueva que hay en él te la doy; a los ojos de los hijos de mi pueblo te la doy. Sepulta a tu muerta».
es.B: «No, señor, escúchame. Te doy el campo, y también la cueva que hay en él. Aquí, con mi propio pueblo como testigo, te lo entrego. Ve y entierra a tu difunta».
es.R: «No, señor, escucha. Te voy a dar el campo, y también la cueva. Mi gente es testigo. Es tuyo. Ve a enterrar a tu esposa».

fr.L: « Non, mon seigneur, écoute-moi : le champ, je te le donne, et la caverne qui s’y trouve, je te la donne ; aux yeux des fils de mon peuple je te la donne. Enterre ta morte. »
fr.B: « Non, seigneur, écoute-moi. Je te donne le champ, et la caverne qui s’y trouve aussi. Ici même, devant les gens de mon peuple qui en sont témoins, je te les cède. Va enterrer ta morte. »
fr.R: « Non, seigneur, écoute. Je vais te donner le champ, et la grotte aussi. Les gens de mon peuple sont mes témoins. C’est à toi. Va enterrer ta femme. »

sw.L: "Sivyo, bwana wangu, nisikilize: shamba nakupa, na pango lililomo nakupa; mbele ya macho ya wana wa watu wangu nakupa. Mzike maiti yako."
sw.B: "Hapana, bwana, nisikilize. Nakupa shamba, na pango lililomo pia. Hapa, watu wangu wakiwa mashahidi, nakukabidhi vyote. Nenda ukamzike maiti yako."
sw.R: "Hapana, bwana, sikiliza. Nitakupa shamba, na pango pia. Watu wangu ni mashahidi wangu. Ni vyako. Nenda ukamzike mke wako."

decisions.choice: I give you the field: the polite opening of a bargain
decisions.reason: Ephron offers more than was asked, the whole field and not just the cave, and offers it as a gift. In the custom of the time such an offer was a courtesy that opened the bargaining; the price follows in verse 15. Taking the whole field may also have bound Abraham to duties that went with the land.

decisions.choice: I give: done in the act of speaking
decisions.reason: The verb is in the perfect form often used for a legal act performed by saying it: "I hereby give".

source.text: וַיִּשְׁתַּ֨חוּ֙ אַבְרָהָ֔ם לִפְנֵ֖י עַ֥ם הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And bowed Abraham before [the] people of the land.

en.L: And Abraham bowed down before the people of the land.
en.B: Abraham bowed again before the people of the land,
en.R: Abraham bowed down again in front of the people there.

es.L: Y se inclinó Abraham ante el pueblo de la tierra.
es.B: Abraham volvió a inclinarse ante la gente del país,
es.R: Abraham se inclinó otra vez delante de la gente de allí.

fr.L: Et Abraham se prosterna devant le peuple du pays.
fr.B: Abraham s’inclina de nouveau devant les gens du pays,
fr.R: Abraham s’est encore incliné devant les gens qui étaient là.

sw.L: Na Abrahamu akainama mbele ya watu wa nchi.
sw.B: Abrahamu akasujudu tena mbele ya wenyeji wa nchi,
sw.R: Abrahamu akainama tena mbele ya watu waliokuwepo.

source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֨ר אֶל־עֶפְר֜וֹן בְּאָזְנֵ֤י עַם־הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אַ֛ךְ אִם־אַתָּ֥ה ל֖וּ שְׁמָעֵ֑נִי נָתַ֜תִּי כֶּ֤סֶף הַשָּׂדֶה֙ קַ֣ח מִמֶּ֔נִּי וְאֶקְבְּרָ֥ה אֶת־מֵתִ֖י שָֽׁמָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he spoke to Ephron in [the] ears of [the] people of the land, saying, but if you, if only you would hear me: I give [the] silver of the field; take [it] from me, and I will bury my dead there.

en.L: And he spoke to Ephron in the hearing of the people of the land, saying, "But if you will only hear me: I give the price of the field; take [it] from me, and I will bury my dead there."
en.B: and said to Ephron, while they all listened, "Please, if you will only hear me out: I am paying the price of the field. Accept the money from me, so that I can bury my dead there."
en.R: Then he said to Ephron so that they all could hear, "Please listen to me. I will pay you what the field is worth. Take my money, and I will bury my wife there."

es.L: Y habló a Efrón a oídos del pueblo de la tierra, diciendo: «Pero si tú, si tan solo me escucharas: doy la plata del campo; tómala de mí, y sepultaré allí a mi muerta».
es.B: y le dijo a Efrón mientras todos escuchaban: «Por favor, si tan solo me escucharas: te pago el precio del campo. Acepta de mí el dinero, para que yo pueda enterrar allí a mi difunta».
es.R: Luego le dijo a Efrón de manera que todos lo oyeran: «Escúchame, por favor. Te voy a pagar lo que vale el campo. Toma mi dinero, y enterraré allí a mi esposa».

fr.L: Et il parla à Éphron aux oreilles du peuple du pays, disant : « Mais si toi, si seulement tu m’écoutais : je donne l’argent du champ ; prends-[le] de moi, et j’enterrerai là ma morte. »
fr.B: et dit à Éphron, devant tous ceux qui écoutaient : « Je t’en prie, si seulement tu voulais m’entendre : je paie le prix du champ. Accepte cet argent de ma part, pour que je puisse y enterrer ma morte. »
fr.R: Puis il a dit à Éphron, pour que tout le monde entende : « S’il te plaît, écoute-moi. Je vais te payer ce que vaut le champ. Prends mon argent, et j’enterrerai ma femme là-bas. »

sw.L: Akasema na Efroni masikioni mwa watu wa nchi, akisema, "Lakini kama wewe, laiti ungenisikiliza: natoa fedha ya shamba; ipokee kutoka kwangu, nami nitamzika maiti yangu huko."
sw.B: akamwambia Efroni, wote wakisikia, "Tafadhali, kama utanisikiliza tu: ninalipa bei ya shamba. Pokea fedha kutoka kwangu, ili nimzike maiti yangu humo."
sw.R: Kisha akamwambia Efroni ili wote wasikie, "Tafadhali nisikilize. Nitakulipa thamani ya shamba. Chukua fedha yangu, nami nitamzika mke wangu pale."

decisions.choice: but if you, if only you would hear me: halting, courteous speech
decisions.reason: The Hebrew piles up particles ("but if you, if only"), as a speaker does when choosing words carefully in a delicate bargain.

source.text: וַיַּ֧עַן עֶפְר֛וֹן אֶת־אַבְרָהָ֖ם לֵאמֹ֥ר לֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And answered Ephron Abraham, saying to him,

en.L: And Ephron answered Abraham, saying to him,
en.B: Ephron answered Abraham,
en.R: Ephron answered,

es.L: Y respondió Efrón a Abraham, diciéndole:
es.B: Efrón le respondió a Abraham:
es.R: Efrón contestó:

fr.L: Et Éphron répondit à Abraham, lui disant :
fr.B: Éphron répondit à Abraham :
fr.R: Éphron a répondu :

sw.L: Na Efroni akamjibu Abrahamu, akimwambia,
sw.B: Efroni akamjibu Abrahamu,
sw.R: Efroni akajibu,

source.text: אֲדֹנִ֣י שְׁמָעֵ֔נִי אֶרֶץ֩ אַרְבַּ֨ע מֵאֹ֧ת שֶֽׁקֶל־כֶּ֛סֶף בֵּינִ֥י וּבֵֽינְךָ֖ מַה־הִ֑וא וְאֶת־מֵתְךָ֖ קְבֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: My lord, hear me: land of four hundred shekels of silver, between me and between you, what [is] it? And your dead bury.

en.L: "My lord, listen to me: a piece of land worth 400 shekels of silver, what is that between me and you? Bury your dead."
en.B: "Sir, hear me. Land worth {{units:about 10 pounds|400 shekels}} of silver, what is that between friends like you and me? Go and bury your dead."
en.R: "Sir, listen. The land is worth {{units:about 10 pounds|400 shekels}} of silver. But what is that between friends? Go ahead and bury your wife."

es.L: «Señor mío, escúchame: una tierra de 400 siclos de plata, ¿qué es eso entre tú y yo? Sepulta a tu muerta».
es.B: «Óyeme, señor. Un terreno que vale {{units:unos 4,6 kilos|400 siclos}} de plata, ¿qué es eso entre amigos como tú y yo? Ve y entierra a tu difunta».
es.R: «Escucha, señor. El terreno vale {{units:unos 4,6 kilos|400 siclos}} de plata. Pero ¿qué es eso entre amigos? Anda, entierra a tu esposa».

fr.L: « Mon seigneur, écoute-moi : une terre de 400 sicles d’argent, qu’est-ce que cela entre moi et toi ? Enterre ta morte. »
fr.B: « Écoute-moi, seigneur. Une terre qui vaut {{units:environ 4,6 kilos|400 sicles}} d’argent, qu’est-ce que c’est entre amis comme toi et moi ? Va enterrer ta morte. »
fr.R: « Écoute, seigneur. Ce terrain vaut {{units:environ 4,6 kilos|400 sicles}} d’argent. Mais qu’est-ce que c’est, entre amis ? Vas-y, enterre ta femme. »

sw.L: "Bwana wangu, nisikilize: ardhi ya shekeli 400 za fedha, ni nini hiyo kati yangu na wewe? Mzike maiti yako."
sw.B: "Nisikilize, bwana. Ardhi yenye thamani ya {{units:karibu kilo 4.6|shekeli 400}} za fedha, ni kitu gani kati ya marafiki kama mimi na wewe? Nenda ukamzike maiti yako."
sw.R: "Sikiliza, bwana. Ardhi hii ina thamani ya {{units:karibu kilo 4.6|shekeli 400}} za fedha. Lakini hicho ni kitu gani kati ya marafiki? Haya, nenda ukamzike mke wako."

decisions.choice: what is that between me and you?: naming the price while seeming to wave it away
decisions.reason: Ephron names his price while saying it hardly matters. Four hundred shekels was a very high price; Jeremiah 32:9 tells of a field bought for seventeen shekels. Abraham pays it without haggling.

decisions.choice: shekel: a unit of weight
decisions.reason: Before coins, silver was weighed out. A shekel weighed about 0.4 ounce (11.5 grams), so 400 shekels was about 10 pounds (4.6 kilograms) of silver.

decisions.choice: about 10 pounds; with the Measures setting, 400 shekels
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the modern weight by default and the original unit as the setting's alternative; Literal keeps "400 shekels".

decisions.choice: between friends
decisions.reason: The phrase implies the two are on friendly terms; Balanced and Readable say so.

decisions.choice: {{units:unos 4,6 kilos|400 siclos}}
decisions.reason: As the English converts to pounds, Spanish gives the metric weight by default: 400 shekels of 11.5 g each come to about 4.6 kg (m2). The Measures setting gives "400 siclos"; Literal keeps the shekels.

decisions.choice: {{units:environ 4,6 kilos|400 sicles}}
decisions.reason: As the English converts to pounds, French gives the metric weight by default: 400 shekels of 11.5 g each come to about 4.6 kg (m2). The Measures setting gives "400 sicles"; Literal keeps the shekels.

decisions.choice: {{units:karibu kilo 4.6|shekeli 400}}
decisions.reason: As the English converts to pounds, Swahili gives the metric weight by default: 400 shekels of 11.5 g each come to about 4.6 kg (m2). The Measures setting gives "shekeli 400"; Literal keeps the shekels.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע אַבְרָהָם֮ אֶל־עֶפְרוֹן֒ וַיִּשְׁקֹ֤ל אַבְרָהָם֙ לְעֶפְרֹ֔ן אֶת־הַכֶּ֕סֶף אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֶּ֖ר בְּאָזְנֵ֣י בְנֵי־חֵ֑ת אַרְבַּ֤ע מֵאוֹת֙ שֶׁ֣קֶל כֶּ֔סֶף עֹבֵ֖ר לַסֹּחֵֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And listened Abraham to Ephron, and weighed Abraham to Ephron the silver which he had spoken in [the] ears of [the] sons of Heth, four hundred shekels of silver, passing to the merchant.

en.L: And Abraham listened to Ephron, and Abraham weighed out for Ephron the silver that he had named in the hearing of the sons of Heth, 400 shekels of silver, current with the merchant.
en.B: Abraham agreed to Ephron's terms and weighed out for him the silver he had named in front of the Hittites: {{units:about 10 pounds|400 shekels}} of silver, by the standard weight the traders used.
en.R: Abraham agreed to the price. While the Hittites watched, he weighed out the silver Ephron had asked for, {{units:about 10 pounds|400 shekels}}, measured by the weights the traders used.

es.L: Y escuchó Abraham a Efrón, y pesó Abraham para Efrón la plata que había dicho a oídos de los hijos de Het: 400 siclos de plata, de curso entre mercaderes.
es.B: Abraham aceptó las condiciones de Efrón y le pesó la plata que había mencionado delante de los hititas: {{units:unos 4,6 kilos|400 siclos}} de plata, según el peso corriente que usaban los comerciantes.
es.R: Abraham aceptó el precio. Mientras los hititas miraban, pesó la plata que Efrón le había pedido, {{units:unos 4,6 kilos|400 siclos}}, medida con las pesas que usaban los comerciantes.

fr.L: Et Abraham écouta Éphron, et Abraham pesa pour Éphron l’argent qu’il avait dit aux oreilles des fils de Heth, 400 sicles d’argent ayant cours chez le marchand.
fr.B: Abraham accepta les conditions d’Éphron et lui pesa l’argent dont il avait parlé devant les Hittites : {{units:environ 4,6 kilos|400 sicles}} d’argent, selon le poids en usage chez les marchands.
fr.R: Abraham a accepté le prix. Sous les yeux des Hittites, il a pesé l’argent qu’Éphron avait demandé, {{units:environ 4,6 kilos|400 sicles}}, avec les poids qu’utilisaient les marchands.

sw.L: Na Abrahamu akamsikiliza Efroni, naye Abrahamu akampimia Efroni fedha aliyoitaja masikioni mwa wana wa Hethi, shekeli 400 za fedha, zinazokubalika kwa mfanyabiashara.
sw.B: Abrahamu akakubali masharti ya Efroni, akampimia fedha aliyoitaja mbele ya Wahiti: {{units:karibu kilo 4.6|shekeli 400}} za fedha, kwa kipimo walichotumia wafanyabiashara.
sw.R: Abrahamu akakubali bei hiyo. Wahiti wakiwa wanatazama, akapima fedha aliyoiomba Efroni, {{units:karibu kilo 4.6|shekeli 400}}, kwa mawe ya kupimia yaliyotumiwa na wafanyabiashara.

decisions.choice: weighed out: silver was weighed, not counted
decisions.reason: Money was pieces of silver weighed on scales; there were no coins yet.

decisions.choice: current with the merchant: by the standard commercial weight
alternatives: silver of a quality merchants accept
decisions.reason: The phrase means silver weighed by the standard that traders accepted, so that the payment could not be challenged later.

source.text: וַיָּ֣קָם׀שְׂדֵ֣ה עֶפְר֗וֹן אֲשֶׁר֙ בַּמַּכְפֵּלָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר לִפְנֵ֣י מַמְרֵ֑א הַשָּׂדֶה֙ וְהַמְּעָרָ֣ה אֲשֶׁר־בּ֔וֹ וְכָל־הָעֵץ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּכָל־גְּבֻל֖וֹ סָבִֽיב׃

records.literal_gloss: And was confirmed [the] field of Ephron which [was] in the Machpelah which [was] before Mamre, the field and the cave which [was] in it and every tree which [was] in the field, which [was] in all its border around,

en.L: So the field of Ephron in Machpelah, which was before Mamre, the field and the cave that was in it, and all the trees that were in the field, throughout its whole boundary around, were made over
en.B: So Ephron's field in Machpelah, east of Mamre, passed into Abraham's hands: the field with its cave and every tree within its boundaries,
en.R: So Ephron's field at Machpelah, near Mamre, became Abraham's property. The field, the cave, and all the trees inside its borders now belonged to him.

es.L: Así, el campo de Efrón que estaba en Macpela, frente a Mamre, el campo y la cueva que había en él, y todos los árboles que había en el campo, en todo su límite alrededor, quedaron traspasados
es.B: Así el campo de Efrón en Macpela, al este de Mamre, pasó a manos de Abraham: el campo con su cueva y todos los árboles dentro de sus límites,
es.R: Así, el campo de Efrón en Macpela, cerca de Mamre, pasó a ser propiedad de Abraham. El campo, la cueva y todos los árboles que había dentro de sus límites ahora eran suyos.

fr.L: Ainsi le champ d’Éphron qui était à Makpéla, qui était en face de Mamré, le champ et la caverne qui s’y trouvait, et tous les arbres qui étaient dans le champ, dans toute sa limite à l’entour, furent cédés
fr.B: Ainsi le champ d’Éphron à Makpéla, à l’est de Mamré, passa entre les mains d’Abraham : le champ avec sa caverne et tous les arbres situés dans ses limites,
fr.R: Ainsi, le champ d’Éphron à Makpéla, près de Mamré, est devenu la propriété d’Abraham. Le champ, la grotte et tous les arbres à l’intérieur de ses limites étaient maintenant à lui.

sw.L: Basi shamba la Efroni lililokuwa katika Makpela, lililokuwa mbele ya Mamre, shamba na pango lililokuwamo, na kila mti uliokuwa shambani, uliokuwa ndani ya mpaka wake wote kuzunguka, vilithibitishwa
sw.B: Basi shamba la Efroni huko Makpela, mashariki ya Mamre, likawa mali ya Abrahamu: shamba pamoja na pango lake na kila mti ndani ya mipaka yake,
sw.R: Kwa hiyo shamba la Efroni huko Makpela, karibu na Mamre, likawa mali ya Abrahamu. Shamba, pango, na miti yote iliyokuwa ndani ya mipaka yake sasa vilikuwa vyake.

decisions.choice: was made over: the sale became legally binding
decisions.reason: The verb (qum, "stand") is used for a transaction that is confirmed and stands firm.

decisions.choice: every tree in the field: the exact terms of a deed
decisions.reason: Listing the field, the cave and the trees within the boundary reads like the wording of a land contract of the time, which named everything included in a sale.

decisions.choice: before Mamre: opposite or east of Mamre
decisions.reason: "Before" (lifne) often means "east of", since a person facing the sunrise has east "before" him.

source.text: לְאַבְרָהָ֥ם לְמִקְנָ֖ה לְעֵינֵ֣י בְנֵי־חֵ֑ת בְּכֹ֖ל בָּאֵ֥י שַֽׁעַר־עִירֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: to Abraham for a purchase to [the] eyes of [the] sons of Heth, among all [those] entering [the] gate of his city.

en.L: to Abraham as a purchase in the sight of the sons of Heth, before all who went in at the gate of his city.
en.B: as his purchased property, with the Hittites, all who had come to the city gate, as witnesses.
en.R: All the Hittites at the city gate saw it happen and were witnesses that Abraham had bought it.

es.L: a Abraham como compra a los ojos de los hijos de Het, ante todos los que entraban por la puerta de su ciudad.
es.B: como propiedad comprada por él, con los hititas, todos los que habían venido a la puerta de la ciudad, como testigos.
es.R: Todos los hititas que estaban a la puerta de la ciudad lo vieron y fueron testigos de que Abraham lo había comprado.

fr.L: à Abraham comme acquisition aux yeux des fils de Heth, devant tous ceux qui entraient par la porte de sa ville.
fr.B: comme un bien qu’il avait acheté, avec pour témoins les Hittites, tous ceux qui étaient venus à la porte de la ville.
fr.R: Tous les Hittites qui étaient à la porte de la ville l’ont vu, et ils étaient témoins qu’Abraham l’avait acheté.

sw.L: kwa Abrahamu kuwa mali aliyonunua mbele ya macho ya wana wa Hethi, mbele ya wote waliokuwa wakiingia katika lango la mji wake.
sw.B: kuwa mali aliyoinunua, Wahiti wote waliokuja langoni pa mji wakiwa mashahidi.
sw.R: Wahiti wote waliokuwa langoni pa mji waliona jambo hilo, nao wakawa mashahidi kwamba Abrahamu alikuwa amelinunua.

decisions.choice: a purchase: bought, not given
decisions.reason: The word stresses that Abraham bought the land with silver. No one could later claim it was only lent or given.

source.text: וְאַחֲרֵי־כֵן֩ קָבַ֨ר אַבְרָהָ֜ם אֶת־שָׂרָ֣ה אִשְׁתּ֗וֹ אֶל־מְעָרַ֞ת שְׂדֵ֧ה הַמַּכְפֵּלָ֛ה עַל־פְּנֵ֥י מַמְרֵ֖א הִ֣וא חֶבְר֑וֹן בְּאֶ֖רֶץ כְּנָֽעַן׃

records.literal_gloss: And after this buried Abraham Sarah his wife in [the] cave of [the] field of the Machpelah before Mamre, that [is] Hebron, in [the] land of Canaan.

en.L: And after this, Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah before Mamre, that [is], Hebron, in the land of Canaan.
en.B: After this Abraham laid his wife Sarah to rest in the cave in the field of Machpelah, east of Mamre (that is, Hebron), in the land of Canaan.
en.R: Then Abraham buried his wife Sarah in the cave in the field of Machpelah near Mamre, which is Hebron, in the land of Canaan.

es.L: Y después de esto sepultó Abraham a Sara su mujer en la cueva del campo de Macpela, frente a Mamre, que [es] Hebrón, en la tierra de Canaán.
es.B: Después de esto, Abraham dio sepultura a su esposa Sara en la cueva del campo de Macpela, al este de Mamre (es decir, Hebrón), en la tierra de Canaán.
es.R: Luego Abraham enterró a su esposa Sara en la cueva del campo de Macpela, cerca de Mamre, que es Hebrón, en la tierra de Canaán.

fr.L: Et après cela, Abraham enterra Sara sa femme dans la caverne du champ de Makpéla, en face de Mamré, qui [est] Hébron, dans le pays de Canaan.
fr.B: Après cela, Abraham mit au tombeau Sara, sa femme, dans la caverne du champ de Makpéla, à l’est de Mamré (c’est-à-dire Hébron), dans le pays de Canaan.
fr.R: Ensuite, Abraham a enterré sa femme Sara dans la grotte du champ de Makpéla, près de Mamré, c’est-à-dire Hébron, dans le pays de Canaan.

sw.L: Na baada ya hayo Abrahamu akamzika Sara mkewe katika pango la shamba la Makpela, mbele ya Mamre, ambayo [ni] Hebroni, katika nchi ya Kanaani.
sw.B: Baada ya hayo Abrahamu akamzika Sara mkewe katika pango lililo katika shamba la Makpela, mashariki ya Mamre (yaani Hebroni), katika nchi ya Kanaani.
sw.R: Kisha Abrahamu akamzika mke wake Sara katika pango la shamba la Makpela karibu na Mamre, yaani Hebroni, katika nchi ya Kanaani.

decisions.choice: the cave of Machpelah: the family grave
decisions.reason: Abraham (25:9), Isaac, Rebekah, Leah (49:31) and Jacob (50:13) are all buried here. The patriarchs' only land in Canaan is a grave, a pledge that God's promise of the land will be kept (Hebrews 11:13).

source.text: וַיָּ֨קָם הַשָּׂדֶ֜ה וְהַמְּעָרָ֧ה אֲשֶׁר־בּ֛וֹ לְאַבְרָהָ֖ם לַאֲחֻזַּת־קָ֑בֶר מֵאֵ֖ת בְּנֵי־חֵֽת׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And was confirmed the field and the cave which [was] in it to Abraham for a possession of a grave from [the] sons of Heth.

en.L: So the field and the cave that is in it were made over to Abraham as a possession for a burial place by the sons of Heth.
en.B: So the field and its cave were transferred from the Hittites to Abraham as a burial place of his own.
en.R: In this way the Hittites gave Abraham legal ownership of the field and the cave as a family grave.

es.L: Y el campo y la cueva que hay en él quedaron traspasados a Abraham como propiedad de sepultura por parte de los hijos de Het.
es.B: Así el campo y su cueva pasaron de los hititas a Abraham como sepultura propia.
es.R: De esta manera, los hititas le dieron a Abraham la propiedad legal del campo y de la cueva, para que fueran la tumba de su familia.

fr.L: Et le champ et la caverne qui s’y trouve furent cédés à Abraham comme propriété de sépulture de la part des fils de Heth.
fr.B: Ainsi le champ et sa caverne passèrent des Hittites à Abraham comme un lieu de sépulture bien à lui.
fr.R: C’est ainsi que les Hittites ont donné à Abraham la pleine propriété du champ et de la grotte, pour en faire la tombe de sa famille.

sw.L: Basi shamba na pango lililomo vilithibitishwa kwa Abrahamu kuwa milki ya mahali pa kuzikia kutoka kwa wana wa Hethi.
sw.B: Basi shamba na pango lake vikahamishwa kutoka kwa Wahiti kwa Abrahamu kuwa mahali pake mwenyewe pa kuzikia.
sw.R: Hivyo Wahiti walimpa Abrahamu umiliki halali wa shamba na pango, kuwa kaburi la familia yake.

decisions.choice: a possession for a burial place: the first land Abraham owns
decisions.reason: The chapter ends with the word of verse 4. Abraham asked for a "possession", and now has one: a small first share of the land promised to his descendants.
